Split two datasets into their common years and the years of one only

Source: R/cwp_split_common_periods.R
cwp_split_common_periods.Rd

Two versions of a dataset (e.g. two releases) are only comparable on the years they both cover: a new release usually adds a year, and a source may cover different years in each version. This function keeps, for each group (by default each source_authority), the years present in both datasets, and lists apart the years present in one dataset only, with their totals. The common part can then be compared with fonction_groupement() or comprehensive_cwp_dataframe_analysis().

Usage

cwp_split_common_periods(
  init,
  final,
  by = "source_authority",
  titre_1 = "Dataset 1",
  titre_2 = "Dataset 2"
)

Arguments

init, final

Data frames in CWP format, with time_start (or year), measurement_value and measurement_unit.

by

Columns defining the groups whose years are compared.

titre_1, titre_2

Names of the two datasets in the tables.

Value

A list:

  • init, final: the rows of the years present in both datasets, for their group;

  • periods: one row per group, with the years of each dataset, the common years and the years of one dataset only, as compact ranges (e.g. "1950-1980, 1983");

  • uncommon: totals by group, year and unit of the years present in one dataset only (dataset = titre_1 or titre_2).

Examples

a <- data.frame(
  source_authority = "IOTC", time_start = c("2019-01-01", "2020-01-01"),
  measurement_unit = "t", measurement_value = c(1, 2)
)
b <- rbind(a, data.frame(
  source_authority = "IOTC", time_start = "2021-01-01",
  measurement_unit = "t", measurement_value = 3
))
cwp_split_common_periods(a, b)$periods
#>    source_authority Years Dataset 1 Years Dataset 2 Common years
#>              <char>          <char>          <char>       <char>
#> 1:             IOTC       2019-2020       2019-2021    2019-2020
#>    Only in Dataset 1 Only in Dataset 2
#>               <char>            <char>
#> 1:                                2021
